# Quick Study Guide: 4.2 Single Document Lookup (findOne())

> "findOne(query, projection) retrieves the first document that matches a given query filter, returning a single document (or null) instead of a cursor."

## 1. Rapid Visual & Core Concept Summary

Architecturally, `db.<collectionName>.findOne(<query>, <projection>)` executes an eager `{ find: "<col>", filter: <query>, projection: <projection>, limit: 1, singleBatch: true }` command, closes the server cursor immediately upon locating the first match, and unwraps the BSON document from the batch envelope.

As depicted in the architectural diagram above, `findOne()` short-circuits collection/index scanning at the first matching record, applies any projection mask (`{ name: 1, _id: 0 }`), and returns a materialized object or `null`—prohibiting post-call cursor chaining. At the storage engine boundary, this sub-topic governs how `mongod` coordinates `OP_MSG` wire frames, WiredTiger `.wt` table and B-tree index extents, and document-level concurrency latches.

## 2. Must-Know Syntax & Mechanics (Top 75% Exam Focus)

- **L-3.1 Command Syntax, Predicate Filtering & Second-Argument BSON Projection.** `findOne(query, projection)` supports the full predicate AST in its first parameter (`{ age: { $gte: 18 } }`) and BSON field projection masking (`{ name: 1, _id: 0 }`) in its second parameter, executing with `limit: 1` and `singleBatch: true`.
- **L-3.2 Eager Unwrapping (`Object | null`) & Runtime `TypeError` on Cursor Chaining.** Because the client driver unwraps `cursor.firstBatch[0]` (returning `null` if `firstBatch` is empty) before returning to the caller, the return value is a plain deserialized BSON object or `null`—never a `Cursor` instance. Invoking `.sort()`, `.skip()`, or `.limit()` on `findOne()` is therefore syntactically invalid.

```javascript
// 1. Eager single-document lookup with range predicate and projection
const doc = db.students.findOne(
  { age: { $gte: 18 } },
  { name: 1, _id: 0 }
);
// Wire RPC: { find: "students", filter: { age: { $gte: 18 } }, projection: { name: 1, _id: 0 }, limit: 1, singleBatch: true }
// Returns: { name: "Aditi" } (or null if 0 documents match)

// 2. Workaround if you need sorted single-document lookup:
db.students.find({ age: { $gte: 18 } }).sort({ age: -1 }).limit(1);
```

## 3. Rapid Revision Flowchart & Cheat-Sheet Table

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    participant App as mongosh Client
    participant Engine as mongod Query Engine
    App->>Engine: OP_MSG { find: "students", filter: { age: { $gte: 18 } }, projection: { name: 1, _id: 0 }, limit: 1, singleBatch: true }
    Engine->>Engine: Stop scan at 1st match & close cursor immediately
    Engine-->>App: { cursor: { id: 0, firstBatch: [ { name: "Aditi" } ] }, ok: 1 }
    App->>App: Unwrap firstBatch[0] -> Return { name: "Aditi" } (or null)
```

| Execution Attribute | `find(query, projection)` | `findOne(query, projection)` |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Evaluation Model | Lazy `Cursor` builder | Eager execution & batch unwrapping |
| Wire Protocol Flags | Standard batching (`firstBatch` + `getMore`) | `limit: 1, singleBatch: true` |
| Server Scan Termination | Scans all matches (unless `.limit()` chained) | Short-circuits immediately at 1st match |
| Post-Call Method Chaining | Fluent `Cursor` pipeline methods | Prohibited (`Object` or `null` returned) |

## 4. High-Yield Exam Traps

- **Exam Trap — Sorted Single Lookup Idiom**: Because `findOne().sort(...)` is illegal in `mongosh`, retrieving the single highest-scoring student requires `db.students.find().sort({ score: -1 }).limit(1)`.
- **Short-Circuit Performance**: When querying an unindexed field where an early document matches, `findOne()` halts the `COLLSCAN` immediately at the first hit rather than scanning the remainder of the collection.
- **Null Safety in Drivers**: Because `findOne()` returns `null` on a miss, application code must guard against `null` before accessing properties (`doc?.name`).
